subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in agent-cancellable hold window for forwarded exec approvals, and if so should it share semantics with the emerging approval cancel path or stay exec-specific?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a broken existing contract; it adds public config and approval protocol semantics on a security-sensitive execution boundary.

options.title: Design a shared cancel/retract contract
options.body: Define a generic approval terminal state that can cover exec retraction and plugin abort cleanup while preserving exec fail-open/fail-closed constraints.

options.title: Keep exec-specific hold/retract
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped `approvals.exec` hold window and exec-only retract method, accepting a separate cancellation contract from plugin approvals.

options.title: Reject the feature
options.body: Keep immediate forwarding as the safety model and address noisy prompts through safer command planning, auto-review, or channel presentation instead.

recommendation.title: Design a shared cancel/retract contract
recommendation.body: Define a generic approval terminal state that can cover exec retraction and plugin abort cleanup while preserving exec fail-open/fail-closed constraints.
